svg.text: Five Flagships loading with both doors open, four waiting in the runway
RUNWAY - OUTSIDE. NO YARD BOUNDARY IN THE SITE MODEL
4400 x 1800 ZONE, MARKED ON THE SLAB
Door swing. Keep clear. 1988 mm headroom.
Lead-in line and traffic lane edge.
Vehicle stand outline and stand number.
Weighing and loading zone, cold chain.
600 mm working strip at every fitting.
1. Morning. HG3 and three Flagships are
already out in the runway, doors shut.
2. Five Flagships stay inside to load: four on
the diagonal and N1 against the east wall.
3. Both doors open on all five, so they load
4. Any of the seven inside leaves at any time.
None of the others has to move.
5. As they clear, the runway four come in,
Five Flagships loading inside, the two HGF
bikes in the north-west corner, and four
waiting in the runway. This is Warehouse
Design V2 exactly as the model has it.
The entry is clear. The diagonal now sits
at v = 2318, nearly a metre south of the 8
September row, and nothing stands between
Any order, both doors, seven vehicles
inside. Each was planned out of the gate
with the other six still standing;
tightest point on any of those runs is 60
One caveat, and it is small: to let D1
out, D2 shuts its north door; D2 needs
D3's; D3 needs D4's. D4 and N1 need
nothing from anybody. That is one door for
a few seconds, not a shuffle.
The runway four keep their doors shut
while they are outside. They open them
when they come in, which is what Scenario

Geometry read directly from Hardware Designs/Warehouse Design V2.3dm and V3.3dm, 9 Sep 2026. Trike positions found from each vehicle's own three wheels, HGF from its rear wheel. All dimensions in millimetres.
